title: Novigi strengthens executive ranks with Apex superannuation leader
full_text:
Novigi has appointed long-time Apex Group executive Andrew Griffioen as chief strategic growth officer, bolstering its leadership team as demand for technology and transformation services continues across Australia’s superannuation sector.
Griffioen will commence in the newly-created role on 1 September, departing Apex after helping grow its Australian super administration business from its origins as IFAA into one of the country’s largest providers.
In announcing the move, Griffioen said he would help drive Novigi’s next phase of growth, deepen client partnerships, develop new capabilities and pursue opportunities in Australia and internationally.
“This next chapter feels like a natural progression,” he wrote. “Technology, data and AI are rapidly reshaping financial services, and Novigi has established itself as the industry’s leading transformation and technology partner.”
Griffioen said he was looking forward to working alongside Ash, Joash and the broader Novigi team while continuing to work closely with many of the same clients, partners and colleagues “just from a different perspective”.
The appointment follows a lengthy career at Apex and its predecessor businesses, where Griffioen held senior leadership positions overseeing the firm’s super operations. Most recently, he served as managing director, super and was a public advocate for technology-led transformation across the retirement savings sector.
During his tenure, Apex expanded its Australian super administration footprint through several strategic transactions, including the acquisition of IRESS’ super administration business and the lift-out of Mercer’s standalone administration operations. Novigi was a technology partner in both initiatives.
Reflecting on his time with Apex, Griffioen said he joined IFAA when it was “a relatively small team with big ambitions” and had the privilege of seeing the business evolve into one of Australia’s leading superannuation administration providers.
“Together we’ve welcomed exceptional clients, built outstanding teams, delivered some of the industry’s most challenging transitions, and continually challenged ourselves to raise the bar for our clients and their members,” he said.
He also thanked former IFAA founder Neil Harvey, along with Apex executives Nick Happell and Peter Hughes, for their support throughout his career.
The appointment further strengthens Novigi’s executive bench as superannuation funds continue investing in large-scale technology, data and operational transformation programs, with consulting firms increasingly competing for senior executives with deep industry experience.
